title: SNS Reversible Retired Feature Pool
authority: Product Owner directives "Permanent Retirement Enforcement -- No Silent Field Reactivation", "Product-Owner Decision Standard" (two authorized removal states), and "Reversible Retired Feature Pool With Explicit Reactivation Authorization" (schemaVersion 2 migration).
purpose: Single authoritative, repository-controlled record of every field or feature the Product Owner has removed from an active RNICA workflow. Retirement preserves historical meaning, persisted values, prior implementation references, and rationale -- it never destroys them. This registry overrides legacy code, dormant persisted properties, old requirements, old tests, old screenshots, archived session records, older branches, alternate worktrees, and merge-conflict defaults. No retired feature may return to the active workflow without a new explicit written Product Owner reactivation authorization naming the exact featureId or clinician label.

statusModel.ACTIVE: Currently authorized for the active workflow. Default status for any feature not listed in retiredFeatures.
statusModel.DEFERRED_FROM_ACTIVE_WORKFLOW: Removed from active use pending field validation or later Product Owner review ("remove for now", "hide pending field validation", "I am unsure this is useful"). Still requires a new explicit Product Owner decision to restore -- absence of a decision is not itself authorization.
statusModel.RETIRED_FROM_ACTIVE_WORKFLOW: Explicitly and permanently removed by Product Owner decision ("not needed", "remove it", "retire it"). Requires a new written Product Owner reactivation authorization to restore.
statusModel.REACTIVATION_APPROVED: A new written Product Owner directive has authorized a specific reactivation implementation, naming the featureId/label, owning section, intended users, current purpose, historical-population policy, required downstream consumers, required Documentation Coverage behavior, required completion behavior, and required tests. Implementation of the approved scope is in progress or pending.
statusModel.REACTIVATED: The approved feature has been restored, implemented, tested, verified (active UI, save/reload, Documentation Coverage, completion, finalization, historical records, downstream mappings, browser behavior), and committed in a dedicated reactivation commit, then accepted by the Product Owner.

precedenceRule: This registry controls over legacy code, dormant database properties, old requirements, old tests, old screenshots, archived session records, older branches, alternate worktrees, merge conflict defaults, and inferred developer intent. A merge conflict must never be resolved by accepting older active behavior for a registered item -- doing so is treated as an unauthorized reactivation and must FAIL the check (see worktreeAndMergeProtection).

reactivationAuthorizationGate.requiredPhrase: A new Product Owner directive must contain the literal phrase: REACTIVATE: [featureId or exact clinician label]
requiredElementsInAuthorization: 1. Feature to restore (featureId or exact clinician label)
6. Whether historical values should populate the restored UI
neverTreatAsImpliedAuthorization: a field still exists in persistence
old code remains in Git history
an old test references the feature
an old worktree renders the feature
a generic requirement engine expects the feature
a prior specification mentions the feature
the feature is considered clinically useful absent explicit authorization
the feature would make implementation easier
the feature is needed to satisfy its own validation rule

reactivationWorkflow: 1. Change registry status to REACTIVATION_APPROVED, citing the authorizing directive.
2. Audit former implementation, current clinical need, current consumers, historical compatibility, documentation burden, and regulatory/HOPE applicability.
3. Return a focused implementation plan before writing code.
4. Implement only the authorized scope -- no incidental expansion.
5. Add or update tests for the restored behavior.
6. Verify active UI, save/reload, Documentation Coverage, completion, finalization, historical records, downstream mappings, and browser behavior.
7. Create a dedicated reactivation commit (never mixed with unrelated work).
8. Change status to REACTIVATED only after explicit Product Owner acceptance.
9. Preserve the complete retirement-then-reactivation history in this registry's reactivationHistory array for the entry -- never overwrite or delete the retirement record.

worktreeAndMergeProtection.rule: Every worktree must read this same committed registry. Before implementation, merge, rebase, or cherry-pick: scan touched files for retired featureIds, requirement engines, Documentation Coverage logic, completion/finalization logic, conditional rendering, new-record defaults, and tests. If a retired feature would become active as a result, FAIL THE CHECK.
worktreeAndMergeProtection.failureReport: Retired feature restoration blocked. Explicit Product Owner authorization required.
prohibited: asking whether to silently keep restored behavior
resolving a merge conflict by accepting older active behavior for a registered item

automatedGuardrailRequirements: Read this registry file directly (not a hand-copied list) in an aggregate test.

For every DEFERRED_FROM_ACTIVE_WORKFLOW or RETIRED_FROM_ACTIVE_WORKFLOW entry, verify: absent from active UI; absent from tab order; absent from Documentation Coverage; absent from completion requirements; absent from finalization blockers; not initialized for new records; not auto-populated; not silently copied forward; retains historical read compatibility when required.
The test must fail if a worktree restores a retired item without the registry status being updated to REACTIVATION_APPROVED/REACTIVATED.
